leakage_rescan.note: query hits are expected and not a real leak: `query` is the original Amazon-C4 user search text, whose entire job is to describe the desired product, so it naturally names category/brand words that overlap with gold_product. smalltalk hits are the ones that matter - Stage 3/4 specifically targeted keeping identity out of generated text.
leakage_rescan.note2: Full per-record hit list omitted from this Drive backup copy for brevity; see the canonical final_dataset_report.json in the repo / HF Hub for the complete 'hits' array.

gold_hypothetical_top_20.note: candidates deliberately never contains gold_product (same exclusion Stage 2 used), so checking gold-in-stored-candidates is trivially always 0%. This instead measures the rank gold_product WOULD have gotten in the same query-similarity ranking had it been allowed to compete - a meaningful retriever-quality diagnostic, not something reflected in the stored candidates field.

get_eval_candidates_gold_replaced_at_20.note: Different metric from gold_hypothetical_top_k above - do not conflate the two. This measures get_eval_candidates(ensure_gold=True)'s actual behavior against the *stored* 100-wide candidates field, where gold_product is always absent by construction (see gold_in_candidates_check). So gold_replaced is always true here, for every record, at any k - this number is expected to be 1.0 and is reported for transparency, not as a retriever-quality signal (use gold_hypothetical_top_k for that).
